claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy.
The feedstock particle-size range is 15–45 μm.
The 15–45 μm feedstock was initially used in HVAF-M3 processing.
An HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance of 300–350 mm will increase FeCoNiCrAl particle velocity.
The proposed spray-distance adjustment will produce a thicker coating than the baseline process.
The proposed spray-distance adjustment will improve coating adhesion.
The proposed spray-distance adjustment will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Increased impact momentum enhances splat flattening.
Increased impact momentum enhances splat fusion.
Enhanced splat flattening and fusion promote coating densification.
Enhanced splat flattening and fusion improve interlayer bonding.
Reducing spray distance increases particle velocity and impact kinetic energy.
Greater impact kinetic energy produces stronger inter-splat fusion.
Stronger inter-splat fusion increases overall coating thickness.
The thickness increase can be achieved without compromising oxidation control.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
The intervention will remain effective for deposition in internal diameters of at least 120 mm.
The resulting bond coat will retain high adherence under high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
Avoiding local overheating is required for the optimized distance to remain beneficial.

contradictions.description: A 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate standoff cannot be accommodated radially within a 120 mm-ID bore. The hypothesis does not specify an alternative axial or external torch orientation that would reconcile the proposed distance with the restricted geometry.

The intervention specifies setting the distance to 300–350 mm, while the mechanism characterizes this as reducing the spray distance. Because the baseline standard distance is not stated, the direction of the intervention is undefined.
